title: cost-pause-batcher-and-quant-throttle-controller
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: Many tenants experience transient unit-econ regressions during sudden traffic spikes where microbatching and cache policies drive up per-token cost without corresponding latency improvements. This PR introduces two cooperating runtime components plus defaults and tooling to automate safe, reversible cost controls: 1) Cost Pause Batcher: a lightweight batcher wrapper that pauses non-critical micro-batches when per-tenant unit-econ metrics (cost-per-request, token-utilization) exceed configured thresholds; it preserves latency SLOs by only pausing batching for request classes marked as 'thrifty' and keeps a small hot-path queue for latency-sensitive traffic. 2) Quant Throttle Controller: a runtime controller that incrementally increases quant aggressiveness (int8 -> int4 simulated pathways / lower-precision kernels where available) when a tenant's cost trajectory breaches thresholds and latency headroom exists. The controller uses a conservative ramp with immediate rollback on quality regressions tied to eval hooks. Changes include: - new runtime modules: runtime/batcher/cost_pause.go, runtime/quant/throttle_controller.go - config: defaults for batching/cache/quant in runtime/config/cost_defaults.go and helm values.yaml - metrics and alerts: unit_econ dashboard widget and alerting rules (console/widgets/unit_econ_dashboard.yaml, monitoring/alerts/unit_econ.rules) - CLI and examples: sdk/python/examples/cost_pauser_example.py, tools/cost-simulate --dryrun - docs: docs/ops/cost-automation.md and an ops playbook for incident response Design highlights: - Decision boundary: thresholds are tenant-configurable with a safe default derived from historical median unit-econ + 2 sigma. - Graceful pause: pausing only applies to non-critical batchable routes; the batcher drains existing in-flight batches and keeps capacity for immediate small batches. - Quant ramping: controller applies staged quant profiles; each stage includes synthetic eval (short run against golden prompts) before promotion. - Observability: new tracing spans for pause/ramp events and token-level cost attribution recorded per tenant. Backwards compatibility: defaults are opt-in via tenant flag; runtime behavior without the flag is unchanged. Testing: unit tests for controller logic, integration tests under perf-canary with synthetic traffic and golden prompt evals were added. CI: full linters, unit and integration tests passed after one iteration to fix race conditions found in initial run. Rollout plan: - Canary (1% tenants) for 48h with aggressive telemetry - Gradual ramp to 25% over 7 days if no regressions - Full rollout gated by cost-savings signal and no increase in quality-regression alerts Notes: this PR is conservative by design (safe defaults, immediate rollback, manual override) and intended as an enabler for automated cost mitigations rather than aggressive cost-savings defaults.

review_comments: Arjun Sinha (2026-02-14): Nice separation of concerns. Can we ensure the batcher pause decision is deterministic under concurrent evaluation? I saw a race in CI on the first run.
Maya Patel (2026-02-14): Addressed: added a small lock around the pause window and an atomic state machine. CI reran and the race is fixed.
Liam Chen (2026-02-16): The quant ramp stage names need to be stable across restarts for telemetry correlation. Suggest including explicit GUID in config for each stage.
Maya Patel (2026-02-16): Accepted; added stable stage IDs and persisted last-applied-stage in tenant metadata so we can correlate events.
Zoe Martinez (2026-02-18): What are the SLO/latency guarantees when batching is paused? Need a short playbook for oncall to force-disable per-tenant behavior.
Maya Patel (2026-02-18): Added ops playbook (docs/ops/cost-automation.md) and a CLI flag to force-disable per-tenant. Updated release notes to call this out.
Liam Chen (2026-02-19): Integration test results look good. One minor nit: add a synthetic eval timeout to avoid blocking controller loop on flaky eval infra.
Maya Patel (2026-02-19): Added 3s synthetic-eval timeout and fallback scoring. Reran integration tests; all green.
release_notes:
- Introduces 'Cost Pause Batcher' to automatically pause non-critical micro-batches when tenant unit-econ thresholds are exceeded.
- Adds 'Quant Throttle Controller' for staged, reversible quantization ramps with rollback on quality regressions.
- New defaults for batching, cache and quant profiles (opt-in per tenant).
- Unit-econ dashboard widget and alert rules.
- CLI tool: tools/cost-simulate supports dry-run scenarios for tenant policy evaluation.
